key_insight: Coarse object masks poorly reflect where meaningful image edits occur; reframing tampering detection as a pixel-grounded, language- and meaning-aware task yields more accurate benchmarks and evaluation metrics.
problem_solved: Addresses the mismatch between region-level masks and true edit signals—many pixels inside masks are unchanged while important edits occur outside—preventing reliable evaluation of vision-language model (VLM) tampering detection.
method: Define a taxonomy of edit primitives (replace, remove, splice, inpaint, attribute change, colorization, etc.) and link them to semantic/language descriptions.
Construct a pixel-grounded benchmark with per-pixel edit maps and paired language prompts/descriptions to capture where and what was changed.
Design metrics that combine pixel-level edit localization accuracy with semantic alignment between detected edits and language descriptions for VLM evaluation.
impact: Enables more faithful training and evaluation of VLMs for tampering detection and image forensics, improving robustness to subtle and semantically meaningful edits and guiding dataset and metric design in future work.
visual_elements: Side-by-side comparison: original mask-based annotation vs. pixel-grounded edit heatmap (highlighting untouched pixels inside masks and edits outside masks).
Taxonomy diagram: visual tree of edit primitives with example thumbnails for each primitive.
Metric pipeline flowchart: input image + prompt → pixel edit map → semantic alignment scoring → final tamper score (with sample metric values).
Before/after example tiles: image, language prompt, ground-truth pixel edit map, and VLM prediction overlay.
paper_title: From Masks to Pixels and Meaning: A New Taxonomy, Benchmark, and Metrics for VLM Image Tampering
paper_authors: Xinyi Shang, Yi Tang, Jiacheng Cui, Ahmed Elhagry, Salwa K. Al Khatib
